title: Āstīka, son of Jaratkāru

words.meaning: in (of) Jaratkāru (his wife of the same name)

words.role: the refrain repeats the last words
marks the end of the formula

sandhi.rule: -aḥ before a becomes -o with the a elided; u before o becomes v; m before n is assimilated (written न्न)

translation.literal: Born of Jaratkāru in Jaratkāru, of great fame, Astīka, true to his word, may he protect me from serpents. “May he protect from serpents — om, homage.”
translation.readable: May Āstīka, the famous son of the sage Jaratkāru and his wife Jaratkāru, faithful to his word, protect me from serpents. From serpents may he protect me; om, homage.

sandhi_exceptions.note: at the break between the two halves of the verse, where the recitation pauses; the witness leaves the vowels unjoined

meaning: The second of the three verses against serpents. It calls on Āstīka, son of the sage Jaratkāru and of his wife, also named Jaratkāru: in the traditional story he is the one who brought King Janamejaya’s sacrifice of the serpents to an end, and so serpents keep their word to spare whoever remembers him (the theme of the next verse). The last words are repeated with om namaḥ, the refrain-form that closes several of these salutations.
in_the_rite: Step sarpa-rakṣā, all three services, after narmadāyai namaḥ.

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: Anuṣṭubh (śloka) with a refrain. The visarga of mahāyaśāḥ stands before astīkaḥ at the half-verse break. Both witnesses spell the name अस्तीक here; in sarpāpasarpa S has आस्तीक.
